company_name: China Taiping Insurance Holdings Company Limited
model: Life insurer FCFE at cost of equity, net debt held at zero (engine route)

inputs.base_revenue_basis: FY2025 insurance revenue (IFRS 17), HK$ million, 2025 AR p.26. Pre-FY2023 'revenue' in the CSV is IFRS 4 total income and is not comparable.
inputs.share_count_basis: 3,594,018,500 ordinary shares, unchanged FY2017-H1 2026; no options, convertibles or awards outstanding (H1 2026 note 13: no diluted EPS presented). Held flat.
inputs.net_debt_note: Net debt held at ZERO per the folder convention for financials. Group interest-bearing debt at 30 Jun 2026 is HK$77.6bn (notes HK$16.1bn + drawn bank facilities HK$61.6bn, H1 2026 p.108), but its interest cost (HK$3.5bn paid FY2025) already sits inside the 'other' line of the pre-tax flow being capitalised, so deducting it again would double-count. Policyholder funds are operating liabilities, not debt. total_debt and cash are recorded for audit only.
inputs.last_fcf_basis: FY2025 NORMALISED free cash flow to ordinary equity: (ISR 24,000 + normalised NIR 6,000 - other -5,137) = 24,863 pre-tax; x (1 - 26% NCI) = 18,399; x (1 - 12% tax) = 16,191 attributable earnings; x 50% FCFE conversion = 8,095. Reported attributable profit of 27,059 is NOT the base: it carries the HK$3.18bn deferred-tax credit (10.6bn utilisation of previously unrecognised tax losses, note 14(b)) and a 14.6bn net investment result that is 2.5x FY2024's.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: CSV OCF minus capex. For an insurer this is dominated by policyholder premium and investment flows and has no shareholder meaning; retained for audit only.
inputs.sbc_source: No share-based payment scheme; FY2018-FY2025 StockBasedComp and EquityAwardTaxes are 0 in the CSV and the only 'share-based payment' hits in the filings are the HKFRS 2 business-combination boilerplate. SBC-zero market: house and street bases coincide.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and quote both HKD. ~90% of the business is RMB-denominated (TPL, TPI, TPP); CSM and EV translate at the RMB/HKD rate and the H1 2026 CSM growth of 6.8% explicitly includes an RMB appreciation effect. RMB depreciation is a direct per-share risk not modelled in the flows; see bear narrative.
inputs.anchors_note: Ordinary shareholders' equity HK$103,638m (HK$28.84/share) and ordinary shareholders' group EV HK$227,606m (HK$63.33/share) at 30 Jun 2026 (H1 2026 p.84). CSM HK$231.4bn. TPL core / comprehensive solvency 128% / 215% at 30 Jun 2026, down from 186% / 298% at 31 Dec 2024.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of EQUITY 12.0% base, built in HKD because the statements and quote are HKD and HKD is pegged to USD: US 10-year ~5.2% (Yahoo ^TNX, 2026-10-09) less the usual HKD-under-USD gap gives an HKD risk-free of ~4.5%; beta ~1.3 x 5.5% ERP = 7.2%; total ~11.7%, rounded up to 12.0% for a state-owned, HK-listed, mainland-China life insurer with a 17% payout ratio and a minority (TPL 24.9%) that sits between the holdco and most of the cash. 1.5-2.0pp above PRU (10.0%, USD) and LGEN.L (10.5%, GBP), the life-insurer comparables in this folder, for China policy, RMB and governance risk. Bull 11.0%, bear 13.0%. One rate across the horizon; risk is charged in the rate and the FCFE conversion, not in both the rate and the growth path.
inputs.lease_treatment: Lease liabilities HK$1.25bn at 30 Jun 2026 are immaterial against a HK$2.2tn balance sheet and their cost is inside the 'other' line of the pre-tax flow; no separate charge.
inputs.nci_treatment: Taiping Life (TPL) is 75.1% owned; TPL's equity-classified capital bonds without fixed terms also sit in NCI. Handled by building the margin on an ATTRIBUTABLE basis: pre-tax normalised operating profit x (1 - NCI share), NCI share 27% base (FY2025 actual 26.1%, H1 2026 27.1%), 26% bull, 30% bear (when life earnings fall, the 100%-owned holdco 'other' costs are a larger share of the whole so the minority's share of what is left rises). The USD2bn holdco perpetual subordinated capital securities (HK$15,987m face, 6.4% to the 2028 call) are a prior claim on ordinary equity whose coupon is an equity distribution, not a P&L charge, so they are deducted at face in equity_bridge and NOT also charged to the flows.
inputs.notes: MODEL: free cash flow to ordinary equity at the cost of equity, run through the component engine with net debt at zero -- the PRU / GL / LGEN.L / IAG.AX pattern for insurers in this folder (SKILL.md routing row: insurer). The owner-FCF DCF is wrong here: reported OCF (HK$61-126bn/yr) is policyholder money, EBITDA does not exist, and capex is immaterial. The pure BVPS x exit-P/B route was rejected as the primary model because IFRS 17 book equity (HK$103.6bn) is less than half the HK$231bn CSM store of future profit and 46% of the HK$227.6bn attributable embedded value, so book is not where the value sits; P/B (0.64x) and P/EV (0.29x) are used as cross-checks in valuation_philosophy. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = IFRS 17 insurance revenue; ebitda_margin_path = normalised pre-tax operating profit (insurance service result + normalised net investment result + other) x (1 - NCI share), as % of insurance revenue; sbc = 0; da = 0; cash_tax_rate_path = normalised effective tax rate (12% base: the tax-reconciliation 'notional 23.9% less non-taxable income' underlying rate was 10% FY2025 and 3.5% FY2024, actuals were 11.8% FY2023, 10.4% H1 2025, 14.0% H1 2026; the FY2024 42% charge and FY2025 -9.5% credit are both the IFRS 17 tax-transition deferred-tax swing, note 14(b)); capex_pct_path is the RETENTION plug = share of after-tax attributable earnings retained as solvency capital for new business and rate/equity risk, so FCFE conversion = 1 - capex/(after-tax attributable earnings): 50% base tapering to 45% from Y6 as growth slows, 35% bull, 60% bear. The low conversion is the single biggest judgment: TPL's core solvency fell 58 points in 18 months to 128% while the group paid out 17% of profit, and the surplus comfort is in comprehensive (215%), not core, solvency. NORMALISATION OF THE BASE (FY2026 Y1, HK$m): ISR 25,000 (FY2025 24,000 x ~1.04; H1 2026 +4.5%) + NIR 6,000 (FY2022-25: -7,480 / -1,838 / +5,831 / +14,583; H1 2026 +9,694; the shift to participating products -- 97.8% of TPL FY regular premium -- moves investment variance into the CSM under the VFA and so should damp but also cap the shareholder share) + other -5,300 (FY2023-25: -5,035 / -5,727 / -5,137) = 25,700 pre-tax; x 0.73 = 18,760 attributable pre-tax = 15.9% of FY2026 revenue 117,880; x 0.88 = 16,510 after tax (EPS HK$4.59, ~5.7x P/E at the current price vs 2.6x on reported FY2025 EPS 7.25); x 0.50 = 8,255 FCFE. FISCAL BASIS: FY0 = FY2025 (Dec); FY2023+ are IFRS 17 / IFRS 9, FY2022 and earlier are IFRS 4 / IAS 39 and are not used as anchors except the restated FY2022 ISR comparative.

equity_bridge.item: Perpetual subordinated capital securities (USD2bn, 6.4%, callable 2028) at face
equity_bridge.note: H1 2026 p.108 and note 26; HK$15,987m at 30 Jun 2026. Equity-classified at the holdco, senior to ordinary shareholders, coupon ~HK$1.0bn/yr paid as an equity distribution and therefore absent from the P&L flows being capitalised. Deducted once, at face, here.

historical_growth.revenue_note: Insurance revenue (IFRS 17) exists only from FY2023: 107,489 -> 111,268 -> 112,267 = 2.2% 2-yr CAGR; H1 2026 +5.3% YoY. FY2022 and earlier 'revenue' is IFRS 4 total income (298-316bn) and a 3- or 5-yr CAGR across the break is meaningless, so those are null.
historical_growth.eps_note: FY2022 EPS 0.778 was the trough (IFRS 4 year, NIR -7.5bn) and FY2025 EPS 7.251 carries the HK$3.18bn tax credit and a peak NIR, so both EPS CAGRs are trough-to-peak artefacts. Attributable profit ex the FY2025 credit (~23,900) still gives a 29.5% 5-yr CAGR from FY2020's 6,549.
historical_growth.equity_note: Ordinary shareholders' equity 90,647 (FY2020) -> 75,506 (FY2022) -> 95,155 (FY2025) -> 103,638 (H1 2026). The FY2020-22 decline is FVOCI bond marks and the IFRS 17 transition, not losses. Attributable group EV per share grew 48.57 -> 58.30 -> 63.33 (FY2024 -> FY2025 -> H1 2026).
historical_growth.fcf_note: Reported FCF is policyholder cash and is not used. Owner-FCF series does not exist for an insurer; the FCFE base is the normalised figure in inputs.last_fcf_basis.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: CSM growth (+4.3% FY2025, +6.8% H1 2026 incl. RMB appreciation), ISR growth (+9.0% FY2025, +4.5% H1 2026) and NBV growth (+2.7% FY2025, +1.4% H1 2026 in RMB) bracket a 3-5% nominal path; the equity CAGR (1.0%) is distorted by the IFRS 17 transition and FVOCI swings and is not used.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR 1.0% vs EPS 5-yr CAGR 31.8%: divergence exceeds 30%. Cause is accounting (IFRS 17 / IFRS 9 transition, FVOCI bond marks in equity, FY2025 deferred-tax credit in EPS), not a change in the business. Neither series is used as the growth anchor.

base.growth_rationale: Insurance revenue +5.3% in H1 2026 (life +0.8% in RMB, P&C and reinsurance flat, RMB appreciation on translation). Fades to 3% by Y6: the agency force is shrinking (57,205 staff vs 61,826), 'Aligning Sales Practices with Regulatory Filings' caps bancassurance volume, and NBV is growing 1-3%.
base.margin_rationale: Attributable pre-tax normalised operating profit / insurance revenue: (ISR 25,000 + NIR 6,000 + other -5,300) x 0.73 / 117,880 = 15.9% in FY2026. Creeps to 16.5% because the CSM (release engine behind the ISR) compounds ~5% while revenue grows 3-4%.
base.capex_rationale: RETENTION plug, not capex: 50% of after-tax attributable earnings (margin x 0.88) retained for solvency capital in Y1-Y5, 45% from Y6 as revenue growth slows to 3%. FCFE conversion 50% -> 55%. Today's payout is 17% of reported profit (27% of normalised), so the model credits shareholders with roughly 2x the current dividend as being theirs.
base.narrative: Steady CSM release, mid-cycle investment result, solvency rebuilt from retained earnings rather than new capital.

bull.margin_rationale: NIR 10,000 (between FY2024 5.8bn and FY2025 14.6bn; H1 2026 annualises above this), ISR 25,500, other -5,300, NCI 26%: 30,200 x 0.74 / 119,003 = 18.8%.
bull.capex_rationale: 35% retention of after-tax earnings (margin x 0.90): solvency stabilises at the H1 2026 level, payout steps toward a 40-50% ratio in line with the FY2025 dividend increase (0.35 -> 1.23).
bull.narrative: Par-product transition completes, investment spread sustained, payout re-rates toward peers.

bear.margin_rationale: NIR 2,000 (FY2022-25 average was 2,774), ISR 24,500 flat, other -5,300, NCI 30%: 21,200 x 0.70 / 115,635 = 12.8%, fading to 12.0% as lower rates and the par shift thin the shareholder share of the spread.
bear.capex_rationale: 60% retention of after-tax earnings (margin x 0.85): TPL core solvency keeps sliding from 128% and the group retains most earnings (or injects capital) to rebuild it; payout stays near today's 17%.
bear.narrative: Low-rate China, weak equity markets, solvency rebuild absorbs earnings, RMB weakens against HKD.

scenario_narratives.base: The CSM (HK$231bn, +6.8% in H1 2026) releases into an insurance service result of ~HK$25bn in FY2026 growing 3-5%; the net investment result normalises at HK$6bn (FY2024 level, well below FY2025's 14.6bn); the holdco 'other' line stays at -5.3bn. Normalised attributable earnings ~HK$16.5bn (EPS ~4.6) of which half is retained to rebuild TPL's core solvency from 128%, so FCFE ~HK$8.3bn. Capitalised at 12% with 3% terminal growth, less HK$16bn of perpetuals.
scenario_narratives.bull: The participating-product transition (97.8% of TPL first-year regular premium) stabilises the investment result at ~HK$10bn, tax stays at the 10% underlying rate, the FY2025 dividend step-up (HK$0.35 -> 1.23) is the start of a move to a 40-50% payout, so 65% of earnings are free to shareholders. Cost of equity 11%, terminal growth 3.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: China 10-year yields stay low and equity markets are flat: the net investment result averages HK$2bn as it did FY2022-25, the ISR is flat at HK$24.5bn, tax 15%. TPL's core solvency keeps falling and 60% of earnings are retained or injected (FY2025 already shows a HK$1.19bn capital injection to a subsidiary), so FCFE is ~HK$4.5bn. RMB weakness cuts the HKD value of every RMB line. Cost of equity 13%, terminal growth 2.5%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 25/50/25, the same as PRU and LGEN.L, the life-insurer comparables in this folder. Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because the TPL core solvency slide (186% -> 128% in 18 months) is a live, not hypothetical, constraint on distributions, and a four-year net-investment-result range of -7.5bn to +14.6bn makes the normalised earnings base itself uncertain. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs the investment spread AND a payout re-rating AND a stable RMB together, none of which a 17%-payout state-owned insurer has yet demonstrated.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value China Taiping as the free cash flow to ordinary equity that its insurance service result and a mid-cycle investment result can support after the capital it must retain, at a cost of equity that prices China policy, RMB and governance risk, with the holdco perpetuals deducted at face. Reported FY2025 profit (HK$27.1bn, EPS 7.25, P/E 2.6x) is not the base: it includes a HK$3.2bn deferred-tax credit and an investment result 2.5x the prior year. Cross-checks: the weighted IV implies ~0.9x H1 2026 book value (HK$28.84/share) and ~0.4x attributable group EV (HK$63.33/share); the 0.29x P/EV at the current price is the market's statement that the EV's economic assumptions (and the state-owned payout record) are not to be taken at face value, and this model agrees in direction while finding the discount too wide.
key_risks_to_valuation: Net investment result is the swing factor: FY2022-25 ranged -7.5bn to +14.6bn; each HK$1bn of normalised NIR is worth ~HK$0.6/share after NCI, tax and 50% retention, capitalised.

Solvency: TPL core solvency 128% at 30 Jun 2026 (186% at Dec 2024). A further slide forces higher retention, sub-debt (whose interest hits 'other') or a capital injection diluting ordinary holders' claim.
RMB/HKD: ~90% of the business is RMB; a 5% RMB depreciation is roughly a 5% cut to every per-share figure here.
Tax: the IFRS 17 tax-transition deferred-tax swings (+9.3bn charge FY2024, -3.2bn credit FY2025) will keep reported profit volatile; 12% is a normalised rate, not a forecast of any one year.

Governance/payout: state-owned (China Taiping Insurance Group), 17% payout, no buybacks, minority at TPL. The FCFE credited to shareholders is 2x the current dividend; if retained cash is never distributed or redeployed at the cost of equity, the value is lower.
Perpetual securities (HK$16bn, 6.4%) are callable 2028; a non-call or reset at higher rates is a cost to ordinary equity beyond the face deducted here.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 15.21-25.96; regular-hours HKEX close, checked against the five prior daily bars (no gaps, no after-hours print).
data_sources.financials: 0966.HK_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, HKD millions, FY2017-FY2025 + H1 FY2023-H1 FY2026); 2025 Annual Report pp.26-29 (consolidated results, segment net operating profit, equity/EV/CSM), p.17 (highlights), pp.56-57 (solvency, leverage, perpetuals), note 14 (tax reconciliation), EV section pp.60-66 (TPL NBV 9,589 after CoC, 21.3% margin); 2026 Interim Report pp.83-86, 108-110 (results, segments, solvency, outlook), note 13 (EPS/shares), note 26 (perpetuals); 2024 Annual Report p.28 and 2023 Annual Report p.26 for the FY2022-23 ISR/NIR comparatives.
data_sources.qualitative: 0966.HK_Analysis.json not present at build time; qualitative judgments taken directly from the FY2025 annual and H1 2026 interim management discussion (life transformation to participating products, agent productivity +73.8%, TPP group-insurance transfer, 15th Five-Year Plan outlook).
data_sources.cost_of_equity: US 10-year 5.24% (Yahoo ^TNX, 2026-10-09) as the HKD-peg anchor; PRU (10.0%) and LGEN.L (10.5%) Drivers files for the folder's life-insurer rate convention.
